attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter essay, endorsed. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The normalised text keeps the core of the sentence but leaves out the 'world tangibly worse' clause and the motive clause about the rich. The sentence is part of a polemical call to question AI executives. It has no metric, no scope and no deadline, so it reads as rhetoric, not a scoreable forecast, even though it says 'will'.

contract.note: The contract fairly says the claim has no single ordinary reading: 'products worse' has no measure, 'drain capital' could mean a bigger AI share or a smaller total, and the other clauses are normative or about intent. Declining to score is fair. Its 'retrospective' label is odd for a prospective sentence, but the result does not depend on it.

evidence.note: Crunchbase data shows AI took about 50% of global venture funding in 2025, up from 34%. That fits only the share reading of 'drain capital'. It does not show total tech capital shrinking and says nothing about product quality. The article is dated Dec 16, 2025, against an available_at of Dec 15. The gap is minor.

reviews.rationale: This compound polemical claim has no deadline, no product scope and no quality measure. 'Drain capital' has two readings that can point opposite ways, and the other clauses are about values or intent. The evidence shows AI's growing share of venture funding, which is context only and settles neither product quality nor whether total capital shrank. The claim cannot be scored.
